rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday way to say that someone lacks talent.

example.english: I’ve always been untalented at singing and go off-key every time.
example.traditional: 我由細到大都冇天份，唱歌次次都走音。
example.jyutping: ngo5 jau4 sai3 dou3 daai6 dou1 mou5 tin1 fan6 coeng3 go1 ci3 ci3 dou1 zau2 jam1

rows.note: Use this especially for a lack of artistic, creative, or intellectual talent.

example.english: He is untalented in artistic creation, and his work rarely leaves an impression.
example.traditional: 佢喺藝術創作方面冇才華，作品好難令人留下印象。
example.jyutping: keoi5 hai2 ngai6 seot6 cong3 zok3 fong1 min6 mou5 coi4 waa4 zok3 ban2 hou2 naan4 ling6 jan4 lau4 haa6 jan3 zoeng6

rows.note: Use this colloquially when “untalented” shades into lacking ability or being unimpressive at something.

example.english: This chef is really untalented; the food they cook is completely substandard.
example.traditional: 呢個廚師真係冇料，煮出嚟嘅嘢完全冇水準。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 cyu4 si1 zan1 hai6 mou5 liu2 zyu2 ceot1 lai4 ge3 je5 jyun4 cyun4 mou5 seoi2 zeon2
